segments.text: American Fork City Council — Regular Session — January 23, 2018:

entities.speaker: Darren J. Falslev
entities.remark-context: COPS grant for a school resource officer

segments.text: Police Chief Falslev said the COPS grant was important because it supported community-policing relationships and would provide an additional officer assigned to the junior high school. He explained that the grant would pay $125,000 over three years in wages and benefits and that the agreement with the school district meant there would be no cost to the City during those three years.

entities.speaker: Kevin J. Barnes
entities.remark-context: COPS grant for a school resource officer

segments.text: Council Member Barnes said he was grateful for the Police Department and remarked that the additional officer funded through the grant would benefit the community.

entities.speaker: Clark P. Taylor
entities.remark-context: COPS grant for a school resource officer

segments.text: Council Member Taylor said he did not think the grant award happened by accident and commended Chief Falslev for what he had accomplished during his tenure as police chief.

entities.speaker: Kevin J. Barnes
entities.remark-context: Police overtime in the Steel Days management agreement

segments.text: Council Member Barnes asked for clarification about the $12,000 in Police Department overtime included in the proposed agreement with the Chamber of Commerce for managing Steel Days and Concerts in the Park.

entities.speaker: Bradley J. Frost
entities.remark-context: State of the City public-safety remarks

segments.text: Mayor Frost reported that the Police Department handled almost 30,000 service calls, made 233 felony arrests, and averaged 1,252 open investigations during the prior year. He highlighted the department's response to domestic violence, including assigning an investigator full time and providing public education; training officers to administer Narcan; joint police and fire training for active-shooter incidents; and Chief Falslev's participation in legislation and a state policymaking board. He said these actions showed that the community was in good hands with police and fire departments that served proactively rather than reactively.
